claims.text: High configurational entropy in HEAs retards the diffusion of key oxide-forming elements such as Cr or Al.
Retarded diffusion of Cr or Al controls the nucleation and steady formation of a dense, adherent protective oxide layer.
AlCoCrFeNi is a typical HEA.
The proposed initial AlCoCrFeNi HEA is homogeneous and has uniformly distributed oxide-forming elements.
High configurational entropy induces lattice distortions and complex atomic interactions.
Entropy-induced lattice distortion and complex interactions impede diffusion of critical oxide-forming elements.
Atomic-scale disorder in HEAs limits inward oxygen diffusion.
Simultaneously slowing outward metal diffusion and inward oxygen diffusion favors continuous growth of a stable, adherent oxide scale.
Selective oxidation of Al and Cr forms Al2O3 and Cr2O3 scales on AlxCoCrFeNi alloys at high temperatures.
The labeled oxide-forming element will diffuse more slowly in the HEA than in a conventional binary or ternary alloy.
The HEA will form a thinner, denser, more uniformly adherent oxide layer than the conventional-alloy baseline.
The HEA oxide scale will have slower overall growth kinetics than the conventional-alloy baseline.
High-temperature oxidation of relevant HEAs can be studied at approximately 900–1200 °C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere.
The proposed entropy-dependent effect is significant only between 900 and 1200 °C.
The effect requires alloys to contain comparable amounts of oxide-forming elements.
Processing history and modest compositional changes can influence oxidation outcomes.
Species transport through the alloy, interface, and oxide layer contributes to high-temperature oxidation, and outward cation diffusion can produce layered oxide films in HEAs.
APT or SIMS can measure diffusion profiles of an isotopically labeled oxide-forming element in the proposed samples.
Cr2O3 has a compact structure and provides strong oxidation resistance.
Increasing Al content can improve the continuity and internal position of Al2O3 scales and thereby improve oxidation resistance in AlxCoCrFeNi alloys.
